claims.text: AOF rewriting rebuilds a smaller recovery representation for the current dataset rather than compressing the previous append history.

Before Redis 7.0, the child writes a new temporary AOF while the parent continues appending new writes to the old AOF and buffers rewrite-period changes; after child completion the parent appends the buffered changes and atomically replaces the old AOF.

Since Redis 7.0, the parent opens a new incremental AOF when rewrite is scheduled, the child generates a new base AOF, and success is published through a temporary manifest that is atomically exchanged to select the new base and incremental files.

For Redis 7.0 and later, if a rewrite fails, the old base and incremental files together with the newly opened incremental file still represent the complete updated dataset, so recovery does not depend on publishing the failed new base.
BGREWRITEAOF is asynchronous; Redis can trigger rewriting automatically since 2.4, and an ongoing RDB background save can cause the rewrite to be scheduled instead of started immediately.

INFO persistence exposes rewrite-in-progress, rewrite-scheduled, last-background-rewrite status and copy-on-write size fields; Redis persistence guidance requires checking rewrite completion and last status before restart, and warns that copying a Redis 7+ append directory during rewrite can produce an invalid backup.

findings: Source-first rereview checked the canonical record and original source question before historical remediation records; the candidate directly answers the AOF rewrite process as a mechanism question.

Current Redis persistence documentation explicitly supports the Redis <7 single-file rewrite flow and the Redis >=7 multi-part BASE/INCR/manifest flow, including the failure-recovery invariant and atomic manifest exchange.
BGREWRITEAOF and INFO documentation support asynchronous triggering, RDB-save scheduling behavior, rewrite status fields, and copy-on-write observability used in the answer.
The revised candidate keeps the Redis 7.0 version boundary explicit, covers the failure path and resource costs, and no longer has a material unsupported factual claim.
